requirements.requirement: Configure the non-root user clusterops on node1, node2, and node3 for key-based, non-interactive SSH authentication.
requirements.summary: Final audits on all three nodes observed UID 1000, a locked password, secure SSH file modes, valid and active sshd, and effective public-key-only authentication with password and keyboard-interactive methods disabled.

requirements.requirement: Each node must reach both other nodes by stable node name without interaction.
requirements.summary: All six directed connections succeeded using batch mode and strict host checking. Each returned the requested node hostname, clusterops as the remote user, and the expected source-node address.

requirements.requirement: Limit clusterops SSH access to the three cluster peers.
requirements.summary: Each node had exactly two authorized keys, each bound to the corresponding peer IPv4 address with from= and restrict. Collectively, negative tests against every server rejected both keyless authentication and an unapproved key.

requirements.requirement: Document topology and basic verification and recovery procedures in /usr/local/share/doc/ssh-cluster/OPERATIONS.md.
requirements.summary: The required file was directly observed on all three nodes as root-owned mode 0644 with an identical SHA-256 digest. Its captured contents include complete topology rows and dedicated basic-verification and recovery procedures.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The captured final state demonstrates a non-root, public-key-only clusterops account, successful non-interactive full-mesh SSH by stable names, peer-scoped authorization, and complete operations documentation on all three nodes.
limitations: There was no fourth, non-peer source from which to try a copied approved peer key; source isolation is therefore supported by the directly observed exact from="peer-IP",restrict authorization state rather than that specific behavioral test.
Lifecycle snapshots use bounded inventories and do not constitute an exhaustive filesystem audit or a persistence test across reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: No executor-caused hygiene problem is visible: all nodes ended without failed services, retained healthy dpkg state, and had no new entries in the bounded temporary-file inventories. The active sshd on the pre-existing port-22 listeners is task-relevant.
